title: Possible critical bug involving Istio configs from isolated namespaces causing blackholes cluster-wide
body:
### Is this the right place to submit this?

- [X] This is not a security vulnerability or a crashing bug
- [X] This is not a question about how to use Istio

### Bug Description

Hello, so we have been having a sporadic issue that has been a hell of a time tracking down, but we know **something** is wrong. 4 times now, over 3 different Istio versions (1.13>1.15>1.17) and 6 months, we've had `BlackHoleClusters` randomly start happening on different clusters and different applications, then fixing themselves. We also use Istio SmartDNS with VIP auto-allocation. This snippet is on all of our deployments enterprise-wide:

```
<redacted-host>/config: |
    proxyMetadata:
        ISTIO_META_DNS_CAPTURE: "true"
        ISTIO_META_DNS_AUTO_ALLOCATE: "true"
```

Here is an example over the past 4 hours:

![image](https://github.com/istio/istio/assets/69006307/d4688f2e-007a-4623-bed6-a3c9614703e5)

You can see they happen(green bars)...go away....happen....go away. Also note the multiple VIP's associated with the same `ServiceEntry`, which is below: (is that expected, that a VIP constantly changes for the same endpoint? Seems odd)

```
apiVersion: <redacted-host>/v1beta1
kind: ServiceEntry
metadata:
  name: elasticache-beta-rocket-fdx-api
  namespace: beta-212697-rocket-fdx-api
spec:
  exportTo:
    - .
  hosts:
    - master.beta-212697-rocket-fdx-api.pvfqf7.use2.cache.amazonaws.com
  location: MESH_EXTERNAL
  ports:
    - name: elasticache
      number: 6379
      protocol: TCP
  resolution: DNS
```

This particular application has had no changes, pushes, nothing all day. We have dozens of applications on this cluster, all with `exportTo: .` on their `ServiceEntry`. Here's what we've discerned so far:

1. The BlackHoleClusters coincide with large Istiod pushes....if I overlay istiod logs on top of the BlackHoleClusters, the red arrows are when the blackholes start, and the blue arrows are when it resolves.

![image](https://github.com/istio/istio/assets/69006307/c577e59f-6169-4553-b29b-f2f007717212)

2. None of the `ServiceEntries` on our cluster are global...so this isn't a "conflict" situation. We enforce `exportTo: .` universally. However, `VirtualServices` and `DestinationRules` are exported mesh-wide, though none of them are related to this particular URL. 

3. This isn't endpoint or TCP specific...this also happens to multiple apps hitting DynamoDB. In this example, you can see it going from working, to blackhole, to working, while switching VIPS (240.240.253.180, 240.240.252.199):

test-rocket-client-info-store-api-59976bcf76-nsp7h istio-proxy [2023-11-27T16:09:42.270Z] "- - -" 0 - "-" 3500 5830 65201 - "-" "-" "-" "-" "52.94.4.150:443" outbound|443||dynamodb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com 100.64.16.133:58816 240.240.253.180:443 100.64.16.133:39484 - - -
test-rocket-client-info-store-api-59976bcf76-nsp7h istio-proxy [2023-11-27T16:13:56.972Z] "- - -" 0 UH "-" 0 0 0 - "-" "-" "-" "-" "-" BlackHoleCluster - 240.240.253.180:443 100.64.16.133:56838 dynamodb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com - -
test-rocket-client-info-store-api-59976bcf76-nsp7h istio-proxy [2023-11-27T17:04:51.606Z] "- - -" 0 - "-" 3469 5799 61007 - "-" "-" "-" "-" "35.71.102.101:443" outbound|443||dynamodb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com 100.64.16.133:53284 240.240.253.199:443 100.64.16.133:51640 - - -
test-rocket-client-info-store-api-59976bcf76-nsp7h istio-proxy [2023-11-27T17:05:30.457Z] "- - -" 0 - "-" 3469 6355 52608 - "-" "-" "-" "-" "52.94.4.158:443" outbound|443||dynamodb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com 100.64.16.133:41732 240.240.253.180:443 100.64.16.133:42652 - - -

4. If I use the `Sidecar` resource, and lock down the namespace to only care about its own Istio config, this problem goes away. So while I technically have a fix and probably should use `Sidecars` anyway, I shouldn't **have** to.


**Based off the above, it seems like Istio configurations (VS, DR, SE, etc.) deployed in other namespaces, which then causes Istiod ids pushes, somehow affect egress traffic in other namespaces, even though aren't related, nor are `ServiceEntries` being exported to anything other than their own namespace.** I noticed the VIP's are changing, one time during a `BlackHoleCluster` I noticed it was to a VIP that wasn't listed in my `istioctl proxy-config listeners...` output....once it started working, it was. Maybe Istiod is changing VIP's but then lagging on pushing them out? My only theory so far.

Myself and 2 co-workers are actively diving into this but are at a loss other than what we've described above. Happy to get any other information, logs, etc. We are worried if this starts happening more often in production.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
I just confirmed what I think is the problem; due to Istio SmartDNS, a VIP is auto-assigned and allocated to *dynamodb-us-east-2-amazonaws.com*. You see this VIP when doing a `istioctl proxy-config listeners $pod`.

As I'm tailing the logs, I see the traffic start blackholing. I go re-run `istioctl proxy-config listeners $pod` and the VIP has changed! Sure enough, if I go back to my logs and re-tail them, the blackhole issues goes away once the egress traffic "flips" over to the right VIP. 

TL;DR - Istio seemingly is changing the VIP in front of my `ServiceEntry` URL, and all my egress traffic blackholes until the sidecar realizes this and "flips" to the new VIP.

***** *EDIT - 04:27pm EST* *******

More proof of this being the case. I'm currently seeing a listener IP of this for

➜  ~ istioctl proxy-config listeners beta-data-share-consent-filter-68d558cf69-55wr8 -n beta-206018-data-share-consent-filter | grep umbeta

`240.240.155.165 9443  ALL               Cluster: outbound|9443||<redacted-host>`

Splunk shows my pod sometimes hitting 240.240.155.**169**, sometimes hitting 240.140.155.**166**. Note how it goes **from working on .166, to blackholing, the back to working?!** Nothing was changed at this time for this app.

comments.author: reporter
comments.body: Update: I can say with 99.99% certainty that creating duplicate `ServiceEntries` in a namespace affect other namespaces. We have 2 teams who use ephemeral environments at our company, so devs can create a PR which deploys our custom Helm chart, which contains a variety of Istio objects (`VirtualService`, `Gateway`, `DestinationRule`, and multiple `ServiceEntries`). Since they are deploying a "variant" of what's already deployed, we end up with situations like this: I had both teams on 2 different clusters both deploy their ephemeral environments today, and the `BlackHoleClusters` started immediately as soon as the Istio objects were created. Mind you, these `BlackHoleClusters` happen in **other** namespaces with `ServiceEntries` for completely different and unrelated URL's. If I had them comment out the `ServiceEntries`, and just deploy the rest of the Helm chart....no issue. **_TL;DR_** - Creating duplicate `ServiceEntries` in a namespace seemingly causes `BlackHoleClusters` in other namespaces for other URL's, neither of which has anything to do with the namespace being deployed to. Specifically, it causes the auto-allocated VIP to switch which is the root of the issue. I have been able to reproduce this multiple times. The only thing I can pinpoint yet is how Istio "select its victims".....dont know why only certain SE's get their VIP's flipped. @participant2 @participant3 In this last case, duplicate SE's for an external URL of one of our API's as well as dynamo caused blackholes in *another namespace* going to *another url*. Nothing was done to this namespace during this, it happened exactly when the duplicate SE's got created.

So every day I get a bit more information....Something must've changed from Istio 1.15 > 1.17, because these devs have been deploying these ephemeral ends since June 30th. These blackholes started 11/7, which is when we started canarying out Istio 1.17.

![image](https://github.com/istio/istio/assets/69006307/9045be65-1df8-4d26-8e79-38321dcef094)

Also, remember.....the BlackHoleClusters aren't tied necessarily to the duplicate ServiceEntries **hostnames**, meaning if I create a duplicate of "sts.amazonaws.com" 3 times in namespace A, that doesn't mean I'll get blackholeclusters JUST in that namespace or JUST for "sts.amazonaws.com"....I might get a BlackHoleCluster for a "dynamodb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com" in namespace B. 

They just seem to cause blackholes *randomly* across ANY namespace and ANY ServiceEntry, that's what's so confusing about this. The developers have since removed all of the duplicates and the problem has gone away. So while they shouldn't be creating duplicates and we have since fixed it, the idea that this could cause random widespread outages is very scary for production. I can't control whether or not devs deploy duplicates, can only offer best practices and hope for the best.

So to reiterate, so far, it *seems* this started *after* 1.15 and the creation of duplicates causes issues on unrelated namespaces and other ServiceEntries.

Hey guys, so I'm reading a bit through the linked PR, some of it's over my head so just a general question; regardless of `ServiceEntry` duplicates, collisions, etc. that might occur, why would they spill over and effect other namespaces? Isn't that the point of `exportTo: .`, to keep any issues isolated to the NS in question? 

If this problem doesn't respect namespace isolation for some reason, then why does applying a `Sidecar` resource seem to fix it? Isn't that kinda the same thing as applying `exportTo: .`, just on the flip side? Instead of saying "don't push this anywhere except this namespace", a `Sidecar` is saying "don't listen for anything else in any other namespaces`. Effectively, those are the same thing, no?

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
short answer: backwards compatibility

longer answer: ServiceEntry handles a bunch of different use cases where the different behaviors make sense

1. exposing an external service --> purely namespaced ServiceEntry makes sense
2. expose a VM service to the mesh with a UX similar to k8s services --> DNS is global (just like k8s service)

My doc explores all these tradeoffs at length, and I still think we should implement it (i.e. DNS search paths) in ambient to avoid carrying that tech debt forward.
